note: Oconto County park at Chute Pond, a 418-acre lake just south of Mountain. The daily campground sits along the Oconto River below Chute Dam, with a foot bridge to hiking trails and the Slippery Rock outcrop; the pond's beach, pier and boat landing are a short walk away. 19 sites take only units up to 20 ft, so check the length posted for each site. Sites 84-100 allow ATVs and UTVs, which ride from there along Lake Shore Lane to the trail system. A separate seasonal campground (sites 1-35) lies across the pond. --Claude
summary: County campground with 70 numbered daily sites plus a group site, 64 electric (22 with 50 A), no water hookups, showers, flush toilets, dump. Reservable on the county's own system (Konect), 2-night minimum, closing 2 days out with walk-up after; $20-35; open April 1 - November 30. The daily loops are on the Oconto River below the dam, not on Chute Pond, so lakefront is proposed down to riverview. Sites 84-100 are ATV/UTV sites (an OHV side, flag only). 67% nightly (70 daily vs 35 seasonal), Google 4.5 (331).
flags: WATERFRONT (stored lakefront, not --AWH, from a 2026-06 bulk sweep): PROPOSE lakefront -> riverview, reviewer's call. None of the 70 daily sites is on Chute Pond. The daily loops lie north of the Oconto River below Chute Dam (county map, confirmed on Esri imagery). The pond shore, with its beach, pier and launch, is reached only from the day-use area. The nearest daily sites, 69 and 70 (the caretaker's) on Chute Dam Lane, are about 150 m north of the pond. Sites 1-35 ('Chute Pond Seasonal Campground') do sit by the pond, but they are seasonal-only and don't earn the value. Along the river: the east loop 39-56 (about 45.1320,-88.4380; electric, 50 A) has pads about 10-27 m from the river behind a tree strip, where the channel is only about 15-25 m wide. Sites 57-61 (non-electric, units up to 20 ft) sit about 15 m from the river at about 45.1333,-88.4423, also behind trees, where the channel is about 27 m wide at the foot bridge. It widens to 40-70 m only in the rapids just below the dam, away from the sites. Under the 30 m rule the stretch beside the sites is creek-sized and nothing fronts it over open ground, so the reviewer may prefer not waterfront. All of these sites are sold by the night.

OHV (flag only; a general campground with an OHV side): 'sites 84 - 100 are designated as ATV-UTV sites'; the map says 'Sites 84-100 allow direct ATV access along Lake Shore Lane west to trail system'. That is 17 of 70 daily sites. The other loops are ordinary camping.
